Currently the Madrasah uses three classes in the evening for Madrasah. The Madrasah currently pay?s rent. But the issue has arisen about rent for the Madrasah when it first opened in 2004. Before the Madrasah opened, eminent scholars gave Mushwerah that the building was not used in the evenings and it would be suitable for evening Madrasah, through this it was then decided by the Chairman that the building can be used without any rent being paid, this was due to the Madrasah being new and to get the Madrasah running, at this time none of the Governors of the school were active in the daily issues of the school. From 2006 due to some issues (regarding the Islamic Secondary school) the Governors of the school got involved and they raised the issue of rent and they decided that rent should be back dated to (2004) and paid to the date of when payment first started (which was 2006). answer: Prayers & Duties >> Waqf, Mosque, Madrasa Question ID: 40065 Country: India Title: A mosque has been built in a nearby village. A person who lives in that village has contributed a sum Question: A mosque has been built in a nearby village. A person who lives in that village has contributed a sum of Rs. three lakh in the construction of this mosque. But this person has no money of his own; the money he contributed belonged to his wife who is a Christian by religion. Now, it is requested to issue a fatwa in this context on whether the constructed structure would be called a mosque according to Islamic Shariah and whether offering prayers in this mosque would be lawful? Answer ID: 40065 Posted on: Sep 1, 2020 Bismillah hir-Rahman nir-Rahim ! (Fatwa: 1102/682/L=1433) If that person has given three lakh rupees with the permission of his wife and the wife has allowed the same considering it good work then it was lawful and right to spend this money in the mosque and as per the Shariah it shall be called mosque and it shall be lawful to offer salah therein. Allah (Subhana Wa Ta'ala) knows Best Darul Ifta, Darul Uloom Deoband, India
